paper: FINRS: A Risk-Sensitive Trading Framework for Real Financial Markets
headline_strategy: FinRS filters daily market/news/filing information into hierarchical memory, uses a GPT-4o direction agent plus a quantity/risk agent informed by scaled Kelly, CVaR, current exposure and volatility, and reflects on a future 1/7/30-day multi-scale reward.
headline_selection_basis: The architecture and ablation identify Risk-Sensitive Reasoning, Financial Insight Prompting, Market News Integration and Multi-Timescale Reward as the proposed full FinRS policy. The shared printed FinPos equations alone are not the novel risk-sensitive strategy.
missing_headline_objects: all domain filtering/analysis implementations and risk-focused prompts
hierarchical-memory allocation, retrieval, promotion/discard and persistence
the direction and quantity/risk agent runtime prompts, responses and parser
the scaled-Kelly equation, scale, probability/odds inputs and portfolio constraints
the CVaR confidence level, horizon, estimator, units and conversion to quantity
the volatility-adjustment formula, window, units and interaction with exposure
the GPT-4o immutable snapshot, decoding configuration, seeds and repetitions
initial account state, trade units, timing, fills, costs, slippage, borrowing and liquidation
immutable provider rows, publication timestamps, actions, positions, PnL and account paths
metric definitions, result generator, raw arrays and uncertainty protocol

cross_paper_lineage.interpretation: displayed-value reuse, not an independent empirical replication

material_paper_conflicts: The allegedly risk-adjusted reward contains no volatility, drawdown, CVaR, Kelly or downside term.
The prose says sliding-window account P&L and horizon scaling, while the equation is an unweighted sum of raw future dollar-price differences.
The reward uses total position rather than action/change and is asset-price-scale dependent.
The decision section introduces future 1/7/30-day differences without an explicit test-time exclusion.
The March-April 2025 test is described as including the November 2024 U.S. election.

rejected_substitutes.route: Treat the three FinPos-identical equations as the FinRS strategy
rejected_substitutes.reason: They describe state/training feedback, do not choose an action or risk size, and contain none of the named risk-sensitive mechanics.
It directly consumes future 1/7/30-day prices and would be lookahead.
Many incompatible definitions and calibrations are possible; choosing one would create a new risk policy.

rejected_substitutes.route: Run a current GPT-4o agent from the prose
rejected_substitutes.reason: No prompts, memory, model snapshot, inputs, sizing rules or execution contract identify the paper policy.

rejected_substitutes.route: Treat the reused FinPos table as independent FinRS evidence
rejected_substitutes.reason: 216/225 exact display matches establish result reuse, not a separate generated return path or policy.

result_policy: No shared paper equation, future reward, researcher-selected risk implementation, current-model prose completion, or reused table result is entered as a FinRS monthly return.
